articles.title: Trained Only on Synthetic Data, It Beats Hand-Built ML (with Jure Leskovec)
articles.description:
#NVIDIAKumo #TabularFoundationModels #GraphNeuralNetworks

In Episode #1047, Jure Leskovec (Professor of Computer Science at Stanford and co-founder of Kumo AI, now part of NVIDIA) joins @JonKrohnLearns to explain how a foundation model that has never seen real data can beat hand-built models on enterprise tables. These models need no feature engineering and no training. Jure pioneered graph neural networks, and since NVIDIA acquired Kumo, his team has released the full Kumo family as open weights under a license that allows commercial use. In this episode, Jure breaks down the four Kumo models for tabular, relational, forecasting and anomaly-detection tasks, explains how they are pre-trained on synthetic data, describes how Biomni came to be used by more than 10,000 scientists within weeks and lays out why he believes human judgment has never been more valuable.

In this episode you will learn:
• (00:00:00) Introduction
• (00:06:18) How Kumo Tabular makes predictions without any training
• (00:16:19) Pre-training tabular models on purely synthetic data
• (00:27:27) Kumo Relational and treating a database as a graph
• (00:54:28) Why human judgment is becoming more valuable

articles.title: 312: Beyond Music City: Nashville's Growing Manufacturing and AI Ecosystem (LIVE from Nashville, TN)
articles.description:
Nashville might be known for its music, but there's more than one kind of talent making its mark on the city.

For this first Nashville recording of Manufacturing Happy Hour, Chris sits down with Simba Jonga, Founder and CEO at Laborup, and Andrew Jebasingh, Founder and CEO at SiteVue AI. Both are building companies focused on manufacturing, using AI to tackle challenges on the factory floor and in the hiring process.

Chris asks what kind of founder and worker Nashville attracts, given its reputation as a city people move to for the lifestyle. Simba points to a young, energized talent base coming through local universities and community colleges. They also discuss why coastal startups scaling production look to Tennessee, and what draws manufacturers there

In this episode, find out:

  • Why Simba thinks Tennessee's startup scene has room to grow, and what needs to happen for more founders to stay
  • How Laborup is finding skilled workers who might never appear on LinkedIn or have a traditional resume
  • What Andrew saw at an Amazon fulfillment center that made him question how factory workers are measured
  • How SiteVue AI spotted a problem on a production line that was costing a manufacturer around $1 million a year
  • Why Andrew believes AI is changing who gets to build software, and why creativity matters more than technical skills
  • How a chance connection at The Lighthouse brought Andrew and Simba into the same Nashville startup community

Enjoying the show? Please leave us a review here. Even one sentence helps. It’s feedback from Manufacturing All-Stars like you that keeps us going!

Tweetable Quotes:

  • “Entrepreneurship doesn’t just live in Silicon Valley or New York. It’s everywhere all across America.” - Simba Jonga, Founder and CEO at Laborup
  • “I think what we will see over the next 20 years is going to be more change probably than what happened in the last 200, which is going to break a lot of people’s minds.” - Andrew Jebasingh, Founder and CEO at SiteVue AI
  • “One in every three software engineers or product designers in Nashville did music before.” - Simba Jonga, Founder and CEO at Laborup

Links & mentions:

  • Laborup is an AI-powered workforce and recruitment platform built for American manufacturing and industrial companies.
  • SiteVue AI is an industrial computer vision startup that uses AI video analytics to help manufacturers recover lost profit through cycle time benchmarking, safety monitoring and workforce training.
  • LaunchTN is an economic development agency in Nashville that empowers innovators across Tennessee by providing capital, commercialization and connections.
  • A3 is North America’s largest automation trade association, representing more than 1,500 organizations involved in robotics, AI, machine vision, motion control and related technologies.
  • Automate is A3’s automation show, with an education pavilion, student robotics competitions, and a list of employers hiring on the floor.
  • Siemens is a global technology leader driving innovation in industry, infrastructure, and mobility through digital transformation.
  • Haley “Zap” Zapolski - is the Founder of The Lighthouse.
  • The Lighthouse is a pre-seed venture investor that backs founders before the traction and headlines arrive, and hopes to get the check when they’re ready to take one.
  • Fathom Digital Manufacturing, offering more than 25 advanced manufacturing technologies under one roof, from CNC machining to injection molding.
  • Software Toolbox is an industrial software company that makes industrial connectivity, DataOps and AI agent products.

Make sure to visit http://manufacturinghappyhour.com for detailed show notes and a full list of resources mentioned in this episode. Stay Innovative, Stay Thirsty.
